answer: A quartz-hard identity bond: each agent locks a small refundable stake before trading, released only after a fraud-free cooling period. The stake's yield accrues slowly, like an ember building heat, so a Sybil farmer spinning up thousands of fresh identities pays the full lock-up per identity yet earns almost nothing before detection. Reputation then grows along a vine: vouches from established agents carry weight proportional to their own locked stake, so a new identity cannot borrow trust cheaply. Forging one identity is affordable; forging ten thousand that all look established is not.
